notes: The current subagent model roster: task-shape-to-tier taxonomy (each tier's `use_when` field) plus the model currently assigned to each tier and its verified capability data. Tiers are named generically (least_capable/standard/most_capable/frontier_escalation) so this file is the only thing that needs editing when the model lineup changes -- add or retire a model here without touching any skill or script that reads it. Update `last_verified`/`source` whenever this file changes.
source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview (fetched live this session; per this user's standing instruction, Claude-model facts must trace to platform.claude.com/docs, not training-data recall)

tiers.use_when: Complete-spec transcription: the dispatching prompt already contains the exact text/code to write, 1-2 files, no design judgment required.

Moderate integration: multi-file coordination, a large-but-fully-specified file, or a spec good enough to follow without inventing design. Default floor for any implementer working from prose (not a fully literal spec) and for review of small/mechanical diffs.
Architecture/design judgment tasks, and review of stateful/multi-step/control-flow logic where a false 'looks good' would ship silently with no downstream check to catch it.

Reserved for escalation only, not a default choice for any task shape: when most_capable has already been tried (e.g. a most_capable review round still missed something, or a most_capable implementer is stuck after repeated fix rounds, per subagent-driven-development's own fix-loop escalation) and the task needs to go one tier higher still. Anthropic's own model-selection guidance positions this tier explicitly for cases where evals on the most_capable tier at its highest effort setting still fall short.
